curriculum: The English-taught Economics and Business Economics BSc at Groningen, programme 50950, has 180 EC. Economics is selected for the generic target because it develops the shared economic theory, markets, policy and empirical core without selecting a firm or sustainability specialism. The dated scheme has twelve 5 EC courses in the common first year, twelve 5 EC courses in the selected second year, and an approved 30 EC minor plus 20 EC of profile courses and a 10 EC Economics thesis in year three. The internship is 15 EC and combines with three 5 EC Minor E&BE courses. At least three of the four named Economics courses are required; one can be replaced with a programme elective. This example takes all four and leaves the minor choice open. The public profile table presents additional thesis entries, including a 20 EC entry. The dated standard Economics scheme and EBB908B10 establish the applicable 10 EC thesis.
progression: The common first year introduces mathematics, economics, accounting and statistics before data analysis and the introductory research project in block 2B. The second-year plan sequences monetary macroeconomics, growth, matrix methods and industrial organisation before econometrics and trade policy in block 2A, and the empirical paper in 2B. The empirical paper is supported by earlier econometrics. Banking builds on the finance, accounting and economic foundations. Year three allocates 30 EC to the minor in the first semester. Dynamic Macroeconomics and Labour Economics are in 2A, and Microeconomics – Choice & Strategy and History of Economic Thought in 2B. The thesis normally runs in semester two, with a semester-one offering also listed. Thesis entry requires 120 EC including all of year one and an approved plan. Prior econometrics and the empirical research paper are strongly recommended and completed earlier in the example.

y2-empirical.prerequisites:
The course builds upon the topics discussed in the course Econometrics for Economics and Business Economics. As such, you have to be familiar with those topics. 
The course is not open for exchange students.

y2-behavioural.title: Behavioural and Experimental Economics
y2-behavioural.prerequisites: Please familiarize yourself with the content of the microeconomics, mathematics and statistics courses that are taught before this course in year 1 and year 2 of the BSc E&BE (or equivalent courses for students from other programs). Please also keep up with the Microeconomics (Industrial Organization) course taught in this block, as some lectures may build on material covered there shortly beforehand.

y3-dynamic.title: Dynamic Macroeconomics
y3-dynamic.prerequisites: Students are expected to be familiar with the content of the courses in Macroeconomics and Mathematics (lcalculus, constrained optimization) of years 1 and 2 of BSc E&BE.

y3-choice.title: Microeconomics – Choice & Strategy
y3-choice.prerequisites: Students should be familiar with the contents of the first year course Microeconomics for E&BE: Consumers & Firms (EBP819B05) and the Mathematics for E&BE (EBP817B05) and Intermediate Mathematics (EBB933B05) in the first and second year of the program.

y3-thesis.title: Bachelor's Thesis E&BE - Economics
y3-thesis.prerequisites: Students must (a) be formally enrolled in the E&BE bachelor program, (b) have completed at least 120 ECTS, including the full first year, and (c) obtained approval for your study program. It is also strongly recommended before starting to working on the bachelor thesis to have successfully passed all previous methodological courses, most importantly Econometrics for Economics and Empirical Research Paper for Economics.

schemeEvidence.thirdYearRules:
Students of profile Economics are required to choose at least 3 of the following 4 courses: Dynamic Macroeconomics (EBB842C05), Microeconomics – Choice & Strategy (EBB852C05), Labour Economics (EBB840A05) and History of Economic Thought (EBB934A05). A maximum of 1 of these 4 courses can be replaced by courses from the table electives E&BE-Economics.

The study abroad programme (foreign minor) must be approved by the profile coordinator of the BSc E&BE before departure and can contain both economic/business courses and non-economic/non-business courses, including no more than one language course in the language of the foreign university (maximum 10 EC).  The courses of the study abroad programme must not overlap with the other courses of the E&BE programme followed by the student. If a student does not obtain at least 30-EC of the foreign minor, a substitution request can be submitted, but only if a student obtains at least 20 out of the 30 EC from the approved foreign minor. A student who has obtained less than 20 EC of the approved foreign minor has to complete an entirely different minor. A student can submit a substitution request to the profile coordinator (via ebe@rug.nl) with a proposal for third-year courses of the E&BE bachelor’s programme to replace the failed course(s). Specifically, replacement courses can only be taken from the Minor E&BE and/or courses not chosen from the 3rd year BSc E&BE courses of the second semester.

It is not allowed to combine parts of different minors.

Fudan DD-students (profile Economics) can choose either the study abroad or the minor E&BE.

Bachelor’s Thesis E&BE-Economics (EBB908B10) can also be taken in semester 1.

The course Analysis of Corporate Reports (EBB116B05) is an obligatory part of the minor Management Control & Accountancy. Therefore, students that take this minor, should choose another elective in the second semester of their 3rd year. 

Students BSc Economic and Business Economics are not allowed to choose the university minor Entrepreneurship.

The Internship for E&BE is a curricular minor option of 15 EC (approximately 10 weeks full time) that must be combined with 3 courses from the Minor E&BE to make it a full 30 EC minor.
